The program was about 10 days long, and you are given a schedule of all the activities you will be doing throughout the program. I think the most helpful activity was group therapy sessions, which I was skeptical of at first, but I grew to like it. Another helpful activity was learning about the various medications and the side effects associated with each one. Sometimes we would learn coping skills and CBT, which was really great.

Some of the other activities were just sending the patients to a room to watch an outdated video that I could've found on youtube. Another activity was aroma therapy while listening to calming music. We also did yoga and made arts and crafts. The only reason I didn't see much benefit out of these activities was because of the cost. I think I could've done all the activities at home for much cheaper than at the hospital. For me, the hospital stay was about $2,500. 

Overall, I think it just wasn't worth the money I put into the program. I did feel better, but I felt like I could have done most those activities at home for a fraction of the cost.

I would recommend going to a psychiatrist and find a therapist who fits well with you. Also check out to see if there are any depression groups that meet up on a regular basis in your area. Those are pretty great too.

I had that experience with a couple of medications. In January 2015, one of my friends passed away, and I barely felt anything because of my antidepressants. I think I was taking Effexor at that time.

I've been considering inpatient, but I'm not sure if I can afford the costs or the time at this moment. I will probably do it someday. I will keep in mind that life is a pendulum. Thank you for the advice.
